intro: Hi! You already know must (harus) and might (mungkin). Today must gets a new job: making smart guesses from evidence, like a detective. The lights are off, so they must be out! You'll learn must be, might be and can't be, and how to show how sure you are. Warm-up: how do you say 'Kamu pasti capek' in English?
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: from b1-modals-advice the learner knows must / have to = harus (obligation), mustn't = dilarang, and may / might / could + base verb = mungkin (possibility). New today: deduction = a logical guess about NOW from evidence. must be = pasti (almost sure it's true), might / may / could be = mungkin (not sure), can't be = tidak mungkin (almost sure it isn't true). Stress that must has two jobs: 'You must wear a helmet' (a rule, harus) vs 'You must be tired' (a conclusion, pasti, NOT 'you have to be tired'). Indonesian 'pasti' in a promise (Saya pasti datang) is 'I'll definitely come', not must.

Common errors and why: *'He mustn't be at home – his car isn't there' -> 'He can't be at home' (it looks like a broken rule, because the opposite of must should be mustn't; but mustn't = dilarang, so for a negative conclusion English uses can't, or couldn't). *'She must to be tired' -> 'She must be tired' (helper word: no to). *'That can be Rina's bag – it's red' -> 'That might / may / could be Rina's bag' (Indonesian 'bisa jadi' pushes learners to can; can be is not used for a guess about one thing now, it means 'sometimes true in general': Jakarta can be very hot in October). Name that can't be works for guesses but can be doesn't: it has to be remembered.

Patterns: modal + be + adjective / place / noun (She must be busy. He might be at the gym. That can't be Rina.), modal + verb (He must know. They must live near here), modal + be + -ing for what's happening right now (They must be having a meeting = pasti sedang rapat). Indonesian traps: no to be (Kamu pasti capek -> 'You must tired'), sedang = be + -ing ('He must driving' -> 'He must be driving'), maybe vs may be (Maybe he's late / He may be late, not 'He maybe late'), and mungkin tidak (might not be, not sure) vs tidak mungkin (can't be, impossible): Indonesian word order changes the meaning, English uses two different forms.

Choosing the degree: strong evidence (several clues, or only one sensible explanation) -> must; one clue or several possible reasons -> might / may / could; the evidence makes it impossible -> can't; a known fact -> is / isn't. Only test clear cases where the evidence points to one degree; might, may and could are equally correct for 'not sure' (may is a bit more formal), so never mark may or could wrong where might fits. couldn't be = can't be (accept it); for 'not sure, maybe not' use might not / may not, not couldn't. British vs American: Americans sometimes say 'He must not be home' (full form) for a negative conclusion; accept it as American English but teach can't be as the safe choice; the short form mustn't be for a guess is wrong.

Limits: present deduction only. No past deduction (must have been, can't have done, might have + past participle), no should / ought to for probability, no will for deduction ('That'll be the postman'), no passive, no reported speech. If a learner asks, say past guesses come in a later lesson. B1 contexts: office (meetings, deadlines, colleagues not answering), KRL, ojek online, airport, campus, receipts and prices in rupiah, Jakarta, Bandung, Bali.

keyPoints.title: must be, might be, can't be: three ways to guess
keyPoints.explanation: must be = pasti (you're almost sure it's true). might / may / could be = mungkin (you aren't sure). can't be = tidak mungkin (you're almost sure it isn't true). Not mustn't be: mustn't means dilarang. After these helper words comes the base verb (no to, no -s): + be + an adjective or a place, + a verb (must know, must live), or + be + -ing for what's happening right now (must be having a meeting = pasti sedang rapat).

examples.en: You started work at 6 this morning. You must be tired.
examples.id: Kamu mulai kerja jam 6 pagi. Kamu pasti capek.

examples.en: He can't be at home. His car isn't there.
examples.id: Dia tidak mungkin di rumah. Mobilnya tidak ada.

examples.en: Listen to that music! The neighbours must be having a party.
examples.id: Dengar musik itu! Tetangga pasti sedang pesta.

id.title: must be, might be, can't be: tiga cara menduga
id.explanation: must be = pasti (kamu hampir yakin itu benar). might / may / could be = mungkin (kamu tidak yakin). can't be = tidak mungkin (kamu hampir yakin itu tidak benar). Bukan mustn't be: mustn't artinya dilarang. Sesudah kata bantu ini datang kata kerja dasar (tanpa to, tanpa -s): + be + kata sifat atau tempat, + kata kerja (must know, must live), atau + be + -ing untuk yang sedang terjadi sekarang (must be having a meeting = pasti sedang rapat).

keyPoints.title: From evidence to a conclusion
keyPoints.explanation: Look at the evidence (bukti: what you see, hear or know), then choose. Strong evidence, or only one sensible explanation → must be. One small clue, or many possible reasons → might / may / could be. The evidence makes it impossible → can't be.

examples.en: The lights are off. They must be out.
examples.id: Lampunya mati. Mereka pasti sedang keluar.

examples.en: Sari's phone is off. She might be in a meeting.
examples.id: HP Sari mati. Dia mungkin sedang rapat.

examples.en: That can't be Rina. She's in Bali this week.
examples.id: Itu tidak mungkin Rina. Minggu ini dia di Bali.

id.title: Dari bukti ke kesimpulan
id.explanation: Lihat buktinya (apa yang kamu lihat, dengar atau ketahui), lalu pilih. Bukti kuat, atau hanya ada satu penjelasan yang masuk akal → must be. Satu petunjuk kecil, atau banyak kemungkinan alasan → might / may / could be. Buktinya membuat hal itu mustahil → can't be.

keyPoints.title: How sure are you? The certainty scale
keyPoints.explanation: From most sure (yes) to most sure (no): is (a fact) → must be (almost sure: yes) → might / may / could be (not sure) → might not / may not be (not sure, maybe not) → can't be (almost sure: no) → isn't (a fact). Careful: mungkin tidak = might not be, but tidak mungkin = can't be.

examples.en: He must be at the office. His bag is on his desk.
examples.id: Dia pasti di kantor. Tasnya ada di mejanya.

examples.en: He might not be at the office. He often works from home on Fridays.
examples.id: Dia mungkin tidak di kantor. Dia sering kerja dari rumah setiap Jumat.

examples.en: He can't be at the office. He's on a plane to Medan.
examples.id: Dia tidak mungkin di kantor. Dia sedang di pesawat ke Medan.

id.title: Seberapa yakin kamu? Skala kepastian
id.explanation: Dari paling yakin (ya) sampai paling yakin (tidak): is (fakta) → must be (hampir pasti ya) → might / may / could be (tidak yakin) → might not / may not be (tidak yakin, mungkin tidak) → can't be (hampir pasti tidak) → isn't (fakta). Hati-hati: mungkin tidak = might not be, tapi tidak mungkin = can't be.

guidedPractice.prompt: Budi is wearing a thick jacket and he's shaking. Complete with must: He ___ cold.
Correct the mistake: That can be Dimas's phone – it's black.
expected: that might be dimas's phone it's black
that could be dimas's phone it's black
that may be dimas's phone it's black
guidedPractice.hint: can be isn't used for a guess about one thing now. Use might, may or could.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with must, might or can't: Sari has two jobs and three small children. She ___ be very busy.
guidedPractice.hint: Two jobs and three children: strong evidence. How sure are you?

guidedPractice.prompt: Which is more sure: 'She must be at home' or 'She might be at home'?

independentPractice.prompt: Think of a colleague or friend who isn't answering your messages right now. Write one guess with might be + -ing.
expected: he might be having a meeting
he might be watching a film

independentPractice.prompt: Your friend hasn't replied to your WhatsApp for two days, but you can see she's online. Write two guesses: one with might and one with can't.
expected: she might be busy her phone can't be broken
she might be angry with me her phone can't be broken
she might be very busy her phone can't be off
independentPractice.hint: might = not sure. can't = the evidence makes it impossible (she's online!).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Rina's gym bag isn't here. She must to be at the gym.
acceptableAnswers: she must be at the gym
rina's gym bag isn't here she must be at the gym
rina's gym bag is not here she must be at the gym
assessment.rubric: Correct: She must be at the gym (must is a helper word: no to). 'She might be at the gym' = 60 (correct English, but the mistake to fix is the 'to', not the word). 'She must at the gym' = 30 (be is missing). Keeping 'must to be' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Dimas mustn't be hungry. He's just eaten two plates of nasi goreng.
acceptableAnswers: dimas can't be hungry he's just eaten two plates of nasi goreng
dimas cannot be hungry he has just eaten two plates of nasi goreng
dimas can't be hungry he has just eaten two plates of nasi goreng
assessment.rubric: Correct: Dimas can't / cannot be hungry (couldn't be is also fine). mustn't = dilarang, so a negative conclusion uses can't. 'Dimas must not be hungry' = 60 (heard in American English, but can't is the standard answer). 'Dimas might not be hungry' = 40 (the evidence is strong, so 'not sure' is the wrong degree). 'can't to be' = 50. Keeping mustn't = 0.

assessment.prompt: It's 6 pm. Pak Hasan isn't at his desk, but his car is in the car park, his jacket is on his chair and his computer is on. Complete with must be, might be or can't be: He ___ in the building somewhere.
acceptableAnswers: he must be in the building somewhere
assessment.rubric: Correct: must be (three clues point to one sensible conclusion: he's still in the building). 'might be' / 'may be' = 40 (possible, but the evidence is strong). 'must' without be = 50. 'can't be' = 0 (the evidence says the opposite).

assessment.prompt: Budi shows you a receipt from a hotel café in Jakarta: '1 cappuccino: Rp 4,500'. You know a cappuccino there costs about Rp 45,000. Complete with must be, might be or can't be: That price ___ right.
assessment.rubric: Correct: can't / cannot be (couldn't be is also fine): you know the real price, so the receipt is almost surely wrong. 'mustn't be' = 20 (mustn't = dilarang). 'might not be' = 40 (the evidence is strong, so not 'not sure'). 'must be' or 'might be' = 0.

assessment.prompt:
Put these sentences in order, from the most sure that the keys ARE in the bag to the most sure that they AREN'T. Write the letters.
A: The keys might be in my bag.
B: The keys are in my bag.
C: The keys can't be in my bag.
D: The keys must be in my bag.
assessment.rubric: Correct: B D A C (are = a fact, must be = almost sure, might be = not sure, can't be = almost sure they aren't). One pair swapped (e.g. D B A C or B A D C) = 50. Anything else = 0.

assessment.prompt: Budi isn't at his desk. You have no idea where he is, but the canteen is one possibility. Write your guess with might, using: Budi / at the canteen.
acceptableAnswers: budi might be at the canteen
budi might be in the canteen
he might be at the canteen
he might be in the canteen
assessment.rubric: Correct: Budi might be at / in the canteen. 'may be' or 'could be' = 90 (same meaning, but the item asks for might). 'must be' = 30 (you have no idea, so you can't be almost sure). 'might at the canteen' = 40 (be is missing). 'maybe at the canteen' = 30.

assessment.prompt: It's 2 am. You call your friend Dimas, but he doesn't answer. Translate into English with must: Dia pasti sedang tidur.
assessment.rubric: Correct: He must be sleeping / He must be asleep (sedang = be + -ing). 'He must sleeping' or 'He must be sleep' = 40. 'He must sleep' = 20 (that means he has to sleep). 'He might be sleeping' = 50 (pasti = must). 'She must be sleeping' = 80 (Dimas is a man: he).

material.title: Guessing from evidence: pasti, mungkin, tidak mungkin

blocks.text:
**Deduction** (*menyimpulkan*) = making a smart guess about **now** from **evidence** (*bukti*: what you see, hear or know). Detectives do it, and you do it every day: *Lampunya mati. Mereka pasti sedang keluar.*

English uses helper words for this, and the word you choose shows **how sure** you are:
- **must be** = *pasti* (you're almost sure it's **true**)
- **might be / may be / could be** = *mungkin* (you **aren't sure**; you know these from the last lesson)
- **can't be** = *tidak mungkin* (you're almost sure it's **not true**)

id.text:
**Deduction** (*menyimpulkan*) = membuat dugaan cerdas tentang **sekarang** dari **bukti** (apa yang kamu lihat, dengar atau ketahui). Detektif melakukannya, dan kamu juga setiap hari: *Lampunya mati. Mereka pasti sedang keluar.*

Bahasa Inggris memakai kata bantu untuk ini, dan kata yang kamu pilih menunjukkan **seberapa yakin** kamu:
- **must be** = *pasti* (kamu hampir yakin itu **benar**)
- **might be / may be / could be** = *mungkin* (kamu **tidak yakin**; kamu sudah kenal dari pelajaran sebelumnya)
- **can't be** = *tidak mungkin* (kamu hampir yakin itu **tidak benar**)

rows.en: The lights are off. They must be out.
rows.id: Lampunya mati. Mereka pasti sedang keluar.

rows.en: There's a long queue at that warung every day. The food must be delicious.
rows.id: Warung itu selalu antre panjang setiap hari. Makanannya pasti enak.

rows.en: Sari's phone is off. She might be in a meeting.
rows.id: HP Sari mati. Dia mungkin sedang rapat.
rows.note: one clue, many possible reasons → might be

id.note: satu petunjuk, banyak kemungkinan alasan → might be

rows.en: That can't be Rina. She's in Bali this week.
rows.id: Itu tidak mungkin Rina. Minggu ini dia di Bali.

blocks.text:
**must has two jobs.** In the last lessons, *must* = *harus*: a rule (*You must wear a helmet*). Today *must* = *pasti*: a conclusion (*You must be tired* = Kamu **pasti** capek). It does **not** mean 'you have to be tired'!
How to tell: is it about a rule or something necessary? → *harus*. Is it a conclusion from evidence, often with **be**? → *pasti*.
**Careful with pasti in promises:** *Saya pasti datang* is a promise about the future = **I'll definitely come**, not 'I must come' (that means *saya harus datang*).

id.text:
**must punya dua tugas.** Di pelajaran sebelumnya, *must* = *harus*: aturan (*You must wear a helmet*). Hari ini *must* = *pasti*: kesimpulan (*You must be tired* = Kamu **pasti** capek). Artinya **bukan** 'kamu harus capek'!
Cara membedakan: apakah tentang aturan atau sesuatu yang perlu? → *harus*. Apakah kesimpulan dari bukti, sering dengan **be**? → *pasti*.
**Hati-hati dengan pasti dalam janji:** *Saya pasti datang* adalah janji untuk masa depan = **I'll definitely come**, bukan 'I must come' (itu artinya *saya harus datang*).

blocks.prompt: That restaurant is full every night, and people wait outside for a table. The food ___ be good.
blocks.explain: Full every night and people waiting: strong evidence, so you're almost sure → must be. can't would mean it's impossible, and mustn't means dilarang.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Restoran itu penuh setiap malam, dan orang menunggu di luar untuk dapat meja. The food ___ be good.
id.explain: Penuh setiap malam dan orang mengantre: bukti kuat, jadi kamu hampir yakin → must be. can't berarti mustahil, dan mustn't berarti dilarang.

id.title: Menduga dari bukti: pasti, mungkin, tidak mungkin

material.title: The opposite of must be is can't be (not mustn't be)

blocks.text:
Here's something that **looks like a broken rule**. You'd think the opposite of *must be* is *mustn't be*. But for a guess, English says **can't be**:
- *He must be at home.* = Dia **pasti** di rumah.
- *He can't be at home.* = Dia **tidak mungkin** di rumah.

**Why not mustn't?** You know *mustn't* from A2: it means **dilarang** (*You mustn't smoke here*). So 'He mustn't be at home' sounds like a rule: *he isn't allowed to be at home*! For *tidak mungkin*, English uses **can't** (or **couldn't**, same meaning). There's no deeper logic: just remember the pair **must be ↔ can't be**.

id.text:
Ini sesuatu yang **kelihatannya melanggar aturan**. Kamu mungkin mengira lawan dari *must be* adalah *mustn't be*. Tapi untuk dugaan, bahasa Inggris memakai **can't be**:
- *He must be at home.* = Dia **pasti** di rumah.
- *He can't be at home.* = Dia **tidak mungkin** di rumah.

**Kenapa bukan mustn't?** Kamu sudah kenal *mustn't* dari A2: artinya **dilarang** (*You mustn't smoke here*). Jadi 'He mustn't be at home' terdengar seperti aturan: *dia dilarang berada di rumah*! Untuk *tidak mungkin*, bahasa Inggris memakai **can't** (atau **couldn't**, artinya sama). Tidak ada logika yang lebih dalam: hafalkan saja pasangannya, **must be ↔ can't be**.

rows.en: He can't be at home. His car isn't there.
rows.id: Dia tidak mungkin di rumah. Mobilnya tidak ada.

rows.en: This can't be the right address. We need number 21, and this is number 12.
rows.id: Ini tidak mungkin alamat yang benar. Kita cari nomor 21, dan ini nomor 12.

rows.en: The shop can't be closed. It's open 24 hours.
rows.id: Tokonya tidak mungkin tutup. Tokonya buka 24 jam.

rows.en: That couldn't be Pak Hasan's car. He sold it last year.
rows.id: Itu tidak mungkin mobil Pak Hasan. Dia sudah menjualnya tahun lalu.

blocks.text:
**can be is not a guess.** Indonesian *bisa jadi* tempts you to say 'That can be Rina's bag – it's red'. For a guess about one thing now, use **might / may / could**: **That might be Rina's bag – it's red.**
Yes, this also looks like a broken rule: *can't be* works for a guess, but *can be* doesn't. Just remember it. *can be* talks about what is **sometimes** true in general: *Jakarta can be very hot in October* (kadang-kadang sangat panas).

id.text:
**can be bukan untuk menduga.** Kata *bisa jadi* dalam bahasa Indonesia membuatmu tergoda bilang 'That can be Rina's bag – it's red'. Untuk menduga tentang satu hal sekarang, pakai **might / may / could**: **That might be Rina's bag – it's red.**
Ya, ini juga kelihatan melanggar aturan: *can't be* bisa untuk dugaan, tapi *can be* tidak. Hafalkan saja. *can be* membicarakan hal yang **kadang-kadang** benar secara umum: *Jakarta can be very hot in October* (kadang-kadang sangat panas).

blocks.text: **British and American:** Americans sometimes say *He must not be home* (the full form) to mean *sepertinya dia tidak di rumah*. You may hear it in American films. **can't be** is understood everywhere and is the safe choice. The short form **mustn't be** for a guess is wrong.

id.text: **Inggris dan Amerika:** Orang Amerika kadang bilang *He must not be home* (bentuk lengkap) untuk arti *sepertinya dia tidak di rumah*. Kamu mungkin mendengarnya di film Amerika. **can't be** dipahami di mana saja dan paling aman. Bentuk singkat **mustn't be** untuk dugaan itu salah.

blocks.prompt: Dimas says: 'Look, Bu Ani is in the canteen!' But you know Bu Ani is on holiday in Japan this week. What do you say?
blocks.explain: She's in Japan, so it's impossible → can't be. mustn't means dilarang, and can be isn't used for a guess.

id.prompt: Dimas bilang: 'Look, Bu Ani is in the canteen!' Tapi kamu tahu Bu Ani sedang liburan di Jepang minggu ini. Apa yang kamu katakan?
id.explain: Dia di Jepang, jadi mustahil → can't be. mustn't berarti dilarang, dan can be tidak dipakai untuk dugaan.

id.title: Lawan dari must be adalah can't be (bukan mustn't be)

material.title: must / might / can't + verb, + be, + be + -ing

blocks.text:
After **must / might / may / could / can't** comes the **base verb** (kata kerja dasar: no *to*, no *-s*). Three common patterns:
- + **be** + an adjective (kata sifat: a word that describes, like *tired, busy, hungry*), a place or a person: *She must be busy. He might be at the gym. That can't be Rina.*
- + a **verb** like *know, live, have, want*: *He must know the answer. They must live near here.*
- + **be + -ing** for what is happening **right now** (*sedang*): *They must be having a meeting.* = Mereka pasti sedang rapat.

id.text:
Sesudah **must / might / may / could / can't** datang **kata kerja dasar** (tanpa *to*, tanpa *-s*). Tiga pola yang sering dipakai:
- + **be** + kata sifat (kata yang menjelaskan, seperti *tired, busy, hungry*), tempat atau orang: *She must be busy. He might be at the gym. That can't be Rina.*
- + **kata kerja** seperti *know, live, have, want*: *He must know the answer. They must live near here.*
- + **be + -ing** untuk yang **sedang** terjadi sekarang: *They must be having a meeting.* = Mereka pasti sedang rapat.

rows.en: Bu Ani knows every street in Bandung. She must live there.
rows.id: Bu Ani tahu semua jalan di Bandung. Dia pasti tinggal di sana.

rows.en: Listen to that music! The neighbours must be having a party.
rows.id: Dengar musik itu! Tetangga pasti sedang pesta.

rows.en: Budi isn't answering. He might be driving.
rows.id: Budi tidak menjawab. Dia mungkin sedang menyetir.

rows.en: Sari can't be studying. Her books are still in my car.
rows.id: Sari tidak mungkin sedang belajar. Buku-bukunya masih di mobil saya.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap: be goes missing.** *Kamu pasti capek* has no to be, so learners say 'You must tired'. English needs **be**: **You must be tired.** And *sedang* = **be + -ing**: *Dia pasti sedang menyetir* → **He must be driving** (not 'He must driving' or 'He must be drive').
**No to:** 'She must to be tired' is wrong. *must* is a helper word like *can*, so: **She must be tired.**

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: be hilang.** *Kamu pasti capek* tidak punya to be, jadi pelajar sering bilang 'You must tired'. Bahasa Inggris perlu **be**: **You must be tired.** Dan *sedang* = **be + -ing**: *Dia pasti sedang menyetir* → **He must be driving** (bukan 'He must driving' atau 'He must be drive').
**Tanpa to:** 'She must to be tired' itu salah. *must* adalah kata bantu seperti *can*, jadi: **She must be tired.**

blocks.text: **may be or maybe?** *He may be late* = two words, may + be (mungkin terlambat). *Maybe he's late* = one word at the start of the sentence. Both are correct, but don't mix them: not 'He maybe late'.

id.text: **may be atau maybe?** *He may be late* = dua kata, may + be (mungkin terlambat). *Maybe he's late* = satu kata di awal kalimat. Keduanya benar, tapi jangan dicampur: bukan 'He maybe late'.

blocks.prompt: It's 1 pm. Budi's desk is empty, and his lunch box is gone too. Choose the correct sentence.
blocks.explain: Happening right now (sedang) = be + -ing: must be having. 'must having' has no be, and 'must be have' has no -ing.

id.prompt: Jam 1 siang. Meja Budi kosong, dan kotak makan siangnya juga tidak ada. Pilih kalimat yang benar.
id.explain: Sedang terjadi sekarang = be + -ing: must be having. 'must having' tidak punya be, dan 'must be have' tidak punya -ing.

id.title: must / might / can't + kata kerja, + be, + be + -ing

material.title: How sure are you? The certainty scale

blocks.text:
Your words show **how sure** you are. **How do you choose?** Look at the evidence:
- lots of clues, or only **one sensible explanation** → **must be**
- **one small clue**, or **many possible reasons** → **might / may / could be** (*might* is the most common when you speak, *may* is a bit more formal)
- the evidence makes it **impossible** → **can't be**
If you **know** the fact, don't guess: use **is / isn't**. Here's the scale, from most sure *yes* to most sure *no*:

id.text:
Kata-katamu menunjukkan **seberapa yakin** kamu. **Bagaimana memilihnya?** Lihat buktinya:
- banyak petunjuk, atau hanya **satu penjelasan yang masuk akal** → **must be**
- **satu petunjuk kecil**, atau **banyak kemungkinan alasan** → **might / may / could be** (*might* paling sering dipakai saat bicara, *may* sedikit lebih formal)
- buktinya membuat hal itu **mustahil** → **can't be**
Kalau kamu **tahu** faktanya, jangan menduga: pakai **is / isn't**. Ini skalanya, dari paling yakin *ya* sampai paling yakin *tidak*:

rows.en: Rina is at home. I can see her.
rows.id: Rina di rumah. Saya bisa melihatnya.

rows.en: Rina must be at home. Her motorbike is outside.
rows.id: Rina pasti di rumah. Motornya ada di luar.

rows.en: Rina might be at home. I'm not sure.
rows.id: Rina mungkin di rumah. Saya tidak yakin.
rows.note: not sure: might / may / could be

id.note: tidak yakin: might / may / could be

blocks.text:
**mungkin tidak ≠ tidak mungkin.** In Indonesian, the word order changes the meaning, and English has two different forms too:
- *mungkin tidak* (maybe not, you aren't sure) = **might not be / may not be**
- *tidak mungkin* (impossible) = **can't be**
Don't use *couldn't be* for *mungkin tidak*: *couldn't be* means *tidak mungkin*, like can't be.

id.text:
**mungkin tidak ≠ tidak mungkin.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia, urutan kata mengubah arti, dan bahasa Inggris juga punya dua bentuk berbeda:
- *mungkin tidak* (tidak yakin) = **might not be / may not be**
- *tidak mungkin* (mustahil) = **can't be**
Jangan pakai *couldn't be* untuk *mungkin tidak*: *couldn't be* artinya *tidak mungkin*, sama seperti can't be.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence shows that the speaker is NOT sure?
blocks.explain: might be = mungkin: not sure. must be (almost sure yes) and can't be (almost sure no) both show the speaker is quite sure.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang menunjukkan pembicara TIDAK yakin?
id.explain: might be = mungkin: tidak yakin. must be (hampir pasti ya) dan can't be (hampir pasti tidak) sama-sama menunjukkan pembicara cukup yakin.

suggestedQuestions: Why can't I say 'He mustn't be at home'?

id.intro: Hai! Kamu sudah kenal must (harus) dan might (mungkin). Hari ini must dapat tugas baru: membuat dugaan cerdas dari bukti, seperti detektif. Lampunya mati, jadi mereka pasti sedang keluar! Kamu akan belajar must be, might be dan can't be, dan cara menunjukkan seberapa yakin kamu. Pemanasan: apa bahasa Inggrisnya 'Kamu pasti capek'?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa saya tidak boleh bilang 'He mustn't be at home'?
Apa bedanya 'might not be' dan 'can't be'?
Apakah 'You must be tired' artinya saya harus capek?

assessment.mdp-1: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Rina's gym bag isn't here. She must to be at the gym.
assessment.mdp-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Dimas mustn't be hungry. He's just eaten two plates of nasi goreng.
assessment.mdp-3: Jam 6 sore. Pak Hasan tidak ada di mejanya, tapi mobilnya ada di parkiran, jaketnya ada di kursinya dan komputernya menyala. Lengkapi dengan must be, might be atau can't be: He ___ in the building somewhere.
assessment.mdp-4: Budi menunjukkan struk dari kafe hotel di Jakarta: '1 cappuccino: Rp 4,500'. Kamu tahu harga cappuccino di sana sekitar Rp 45.000. Lengkapi dengan must be, might be atau can't be: That price ___ right.
assessment.mdp-5:
Urutkan kalimat-kalimat ini, dari yang paling yakin kuncinya ADA di tas sampai yang paling yakin kuncinya TIDAK ADA. Tulis hurufnya.
A: The keys might be in my bag.
B: The keys are in my bag.
C: The keys can't be in my bag.
D: The keys must be in my bag.
assessment.mdp-6: Budi tidak ada di mejanya. Kamu sama sekali tidak tahu dia di mana, tapi kantin salah satu kemungkinannya. Tulis dugaanmu dalam bahasa Inggris dengan might, memakai: Budi / at the canteen.
assessment.mdp-7: Jam 2 pagi. Kamu menelepon temanmu Dimas, tapi dia tidak menjawab. Terjemahkan ke bahasa Inggris dengan must: Dia pasti sedang tidur.
